sections.name: File setup, NotificationModule
sections.title: Notification feature wiring and queue settings
sections.what: Creates the background queue with retry settings, then lists the controller, worker, services and shares the notification and mail services with the rest of the app.
sections.why: Likely reason: sending is moved to a background worker so user requests stay fast and failed sends can retry.
sections.watch_out: The retry settings are set here and again in the notification service when each job is added, so changing one may not change the other.

summary: Groups the notification controller, services, the background delivery worker and the email service into one module.
purpose: Tells the app how the notification pieces fit together, including the job queue named notifications.
why: Likely reason: delivery runs in the background so slow sends do not block the user's request.
how: Registers a queue called notifications with three tries and exponential waiting between tries, removes finished jobs, then lists the controller, services and worker. It marks the module global and shares the notification and mail services.
inputs: None directly. It is read when the app starts.
outputs: A module the main app loads.
risks: Because the module is global, the shared services are available everywhere, which can hide where they are used.
debug: If notifications are queued but never sent, check the queue is registered and that the worker is listed here. Check the Redis connection used by the queue.
